Ran the numbers before you commit the extra $800. Short version: the "crushing it" read is real on efficiency, but there's no data showing what more dollars buys, because channel B spend has never moved.

**What the data shows (channel B, $800/quarter, holding steady for 6 straight quarters: Q1'25 through Q1'26):**
- Leads: 23-25/quarter, roughly flat
- Won rate: 24%-52%, trending up (Q1'26 was 52%, the best of any channel)
- Won jobs: 6, 10, 10, 8, 12 → average 9.2/quarter
- Revenue from those jobs: avg **$11,676/quarter**
- Gross profit: avg **$5,230/quarter**
- Implied cost per won job: **~$87** (vs channel A's ~$106 on $1,000/quarter spend, ~9.4 won jobs/quarter)

So yes, B is cheaper per acquisition and converting better than A. That part checks out.

**The gap: spend has been perfectly flat at $800/quarter every single quarter in the data.** There is not one historical data point at any other spend level for either channel. That means I have zero evidence for what happens if you push $1,600/quarter through it. It could be:
- A pay-for-volume channel where more dollars buys roughly proportional leads (in which case, doubling spend might roughly double the ~9 won jobs and ~$5,230 GP, i.e. an incremental quarter's worth for another $800), or
- A flat retainer/placement fee (the ledger shows it as one lump $800 line each quarter, not a scaling spend), in which case extra dollars might buy nothing more from the same vendor and you'd need a second slot, a new territory, or a tier upgrade to get incremental volume at all.

I can't tell which of those it is from this data.

**One more flag:** Q2 2026 (the most recent quarter, with a big lead surge: A leads jumped to 100, B to 40, plus 61 referral leads appearing) has suspiciously round revenue/cost figures ($20,000/$12,000/$8,000 for A, $27,000/$16,200/$10,800 for B, $95,200/$57,120/$38,080 for referral) versus every other quarter's realistic decimal figures. That looks like placeholder/estimated data, not actuals, so I excluded it from the baseline above and wouldn't use it to justify the spend increase.

**Recommendation:** before committing, confirm with whoever runs channel B whether the extra $800 buys more volume or just extends the same flat placement. If it does scale, treat this quarter as a live test and compare actual won-jobs/revenue/GP against the $5,230 GP baseline above, that's the only way to actually measure the marginal return since the history can't tell you.

ANSWER: Channel B's historical efficiency edge is real (lower cost per won job, higher conversion than channel A), but spend has been flat at $800/quarter for 6 straight quarters so there's no data showing what an incremental $800 actually buys; confirm with the vendor whether it scales before committing, and treat this quarter as a measured test against the ~$5,230/quarter gross profit baseline.
